header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (AuroraCloud Head of Partnerships), Tom Rhee (AuroraCloud Platform Eng), Priya Gupta (AuroraCloud Security)
Notes: partner technical sync covering marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for joint solution, POC scope and security/compliance questions.
summary: High-level technical sync between Redwood and AuroraCloud focused on marketplace listing artifacts, network and security constraints for a joint reference architecture, and next steps for a POC. Key concerns: VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs, marketplace acceptance timelines, and competitive positioning. Action items assigned and POC benchmark to be run.
topics: Reference architecture: VPC & peering, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
POC scope & benchmarks: throughput/latency targets, model variants
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone for joining, uh we'll get started in a minute. This is Sofia from Redwood, AE on this account.
[00:07] Maya Patel: hey thanks Sofia, excited to sync. we've got Tom and Priya here as well.
[00:12] Liam Chen: hi all liam from the se team, i'll drive the tech bits, run through integration options and benchmark plan.
[00:19] Tom Rhee: tom here, platform eng, i'll be handling the network and infra questions.
[00:25] Priya Gupta: priya, security architect, i'll be focused on compliance scope.
[00:30] Sofia Martinez: cool, agenda — marketplace listing requirements, reference arch for a joint solution (we're thinking Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private behind auroracloud marketplace), security scoped items, then POC/benchmarks and next steps. any additions?
[00:44] Maya Patel: that sounds right, timeline is tight — we'd like a listing live in MAY if possible.
[00:49] Sofia Martinez: got it, we'll talk timeline at the end.
[00:52] Liam Chen: quick note on terminology — when i say dedicated it's reserved GPU capacity, private is vpc/on prem like you mentioned. sometimes the transcript or docs say "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Conzole" so ignore typos.
[01:10] Tom Rhee: good, on networking, our marketplace requires either a public endpoint or a marketplace-provisioned private link. For security reasons we prefer private link / vpc peering. what are our options?
[01:25] Liam Chen: we support VPC peering and private link; in Dedicated mode you can peering directly into Redwood Dedicated VPCs — for Private it's customer-managed networking. We also do token-based auth and can integrate with your SAML SSO for provisioning.
[01:40] Priya Gupta: on encryption, we need to know about KMS — can Redwood use our KMS, and do audit logs cover model invocation and token IDs?
[01:51] Liam Chen: yes we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; for Hosted API we have server-side encryption and can negotiate bring-your-own-key for enterprise. Audit logs capture request metadata: model id, route, latency, but sometimes PII in logs is redacted — we can configure retention and export to your logging bucket.
[02:12] Priya Gupta: what's the retention window and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[02:17] Liam Chen: retention's configurable, typical is 90 days in platform, but for Private you control it; we export to S3/Cloud Storage and push to SIEM via connector. we'll document exact fields and example schema.
[02:33] Maya Patel: marketplace listing — what's required from our side? screenshots, listing copy, support contact, pricing plan?
[02:40] Sofia Martinez: yes checklist: listing description, screenshots (console flows), pricing tiers (per-seat/per-hour or committed), support SLAs, security documents (SOC2 report, infra diagram), and a reference architecture diagram. we'll share a template.
[02:55] Tom Rhee: on the reference arch, we need clarity on deployment options. If a customer picks marketplace listing that spins up Dedicated instances, how does billing and provisioning tie back to AuroraCloud? who owns the node lifecycle?
[03:10] Liam Chen: two models: 1) marketplace listing that references Redwood as a SaaS offering — listing links to Redwood-managed service and Aurora handles billing redirect or referral; 2) joint marketplace integration where Aurora provisions infra and Redwood's package runs as a managed tenant — provisioning flow can be automated via our infra API. We'll need to nail the integration points for provisioning and billing.
[03:33] Maya Patel: that second option is interesting — customers want single-pane provisioning. what's required for automation?
[03:38] Liam Chen: we'll need API keys, a provisioning webhook, and possibly a small connector lambda inside Aurora to call Redwood's provisioning API. also network details for VPC peering and initial account mapping.
[03:52] Priya Gupta: ok but from compliance perspective we need to vet the provisioning flow and ensure least privilege and that keys are rotated. also need SOC2 docs.
[04:03] Sofia Martinez: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and compliance pack; priya, i'll include our compliance contact.
[04:10] Priya Gupta: excellent.
[04:12] Tom Rhee: about POC — we want to run benchmarks on representative workloads. latency under 200ms for short prompts is a hard ask for our customers, can you hit that?
[04:24] Liam Chen: depends on model & infra. For small models and Redwood Dedicated in the same region we commonly see <100ms token latency for short seq, but for larger models 200ms is optimistic. We'll propose a bench plan: synthetic qps and a replay of your traffic.
[04:40] Maya Patel: what metrics will you provide? throughput (tokens/s), p99 latency, cost per 1000 tokens?
[04:47] Liam Chen: yes we'll provide p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and estimated unit cost using your target quantization/profile. we'll include KV cache hit rates where applicable.
[04:58] Tom Rhee: ok, we'll provide a 48hr traffic capture and a small sample prompt set.
[05:04] Sofia Martinez: perfect. i'll open an action item for sharing the bench plan and artifacts.
[05:10] Maya Patel: Anything on the marketplace acceptance criteria? sometimes Marketplace teams want a security review and a minimum number of support hours.
[05:18] Sofia Martinez: standard marketplace acceptance: listing copy + support contact, basic security attestation (SOC2), integration test results (smoke tests), and a demo artifact. For Aurora's marketplace there may be additional steps — we should align with your partner ops checklist.
[05:33] Maya Patel: yes we'll share partner ops checklist after this call.
[05:37] Liam Chen: one more technical note — for Private deployments we can do BYO-KMS and direct audit log export, which makes acceptance easier. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide equivalent controls but need to map the compliance boundary.
[05:52] Priya Gupta: what's the typical SLA? and are there runbooks?
[05:57] Sofia Martinez: our Dedicated customers have SLA options; we'll share an SLA summary and runbooks — in Redwood Console we have per-route metrics and tracing hooks to help with debugging.
[06:08] Tom Rhee: curious about model upgrades — how do rollouts work? we want stable API versions and the ability to pin model variants per deployment.
[06:17] Liam Chen: we support model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B). You can pin by model version in the provisioning payload. For marketplace listings we recommend exposing options for model size and quantization profiles.
[06:31] Maya Patel: on the go-to-market side, what's the co-branding allowed on the listing?
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: we typically co-brand, Aurora logo + Redwood description; we can share guidelines.
[06:40] Maya Patel: great.
[06:42] [brief silence, 06:50]
[06:50] Sofia Martinez: let's walk through the immediate asks: 1) we'll share marketplace listing template, 2) we need your VPC constraints and region list, 3) we'll run benchmarks once you provide traffic samples.
[07:04] Tom Rhee: network details — we have restrictions on cross-region peering; can you support multi-region deployment?
[07:12] Liam Chen: yes, our routing supports region affinity; we can route by policy and fallback to other regions if capacity constrained. there are latency tradeoffs though.
[07:25] Priya Gupta: for the SOC2 scope — do you include data retention and deletion controls?
[07:31] Liam Chen: yes, we have retention controls, deletion API, and can automate deletions per customer policy in Private deployments; hosted requires coordination.
[07:44] Maya Patel: competitors question — customers sometimes ask whether this is similar to CloudPeak's marketplace offering. how do we position?
[07:52] Sofia Martinez: we emphasize production economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and strong observability (per-route cost breakdowns). we can provide benchmark docs to help Aurora with comparative positioning.
[08:07] Tom Rhee: ok, on the POC infra — do you have terraform modules or helm charts to provision connectors?
[08:15] Liam Chen: we provide terraform modules for provisioning dedicated capacity and a small connector repo for the provisioning webhook. we'll hand over sample templates.
[08:26] Maya Patel: let's confirm timeline: if we get the listing assets by 04-24 and network diagrams by 04-23, can we aim for a POC start week of 05-04 and listing go-live mid-May?
[08:38] Sofia Martinez: that's feasible pending successful POC and partner ops sign-off.
[08:43] Priya Gupta: will our security team need to do an on-site review or is remote docs fine?
[08:48] Liam Chen: remote review plus a short security questionnaire is usually enough; if you require an on-site we can discuss.
[08:56] Tom Rhee: any common gotchas you've seen?
[08:59] Liam Chen: often network egress rules and proxy configs cause issues; also mismatch in KMS policies — we'll include a validation checklist.
[09:12] Maya Patel: awesome, can you share the draft listing and the reference arch?
[09:16] Sofia Martinez: yes, action items recorded, i'll send the draft listing and template by Friday.
[09:21] Liam Chen: i'll own the benchmark plan and initial tests.
[09:24] Priya Gupta: i'll coordinate SOC2 and security questionnaire with our team.
[09:29] Sofia Martinez: wrap-up: Next steps — share artifacts, run bench once we have traffic capture, schedule POC kickoff for week of May 4. any final Qs?
[09:39] Maya Patel: none, thanks everyone.
[09:41] Tom Rhee: thanks.
[09:43] Sofia Martinez: thanks all, we'll follow up in email. Bye.
[52:00] call ended (approx)
Notes: minor transcription errors present; speaker labels approximate.
